page: Vultr vhp-1c-1gb-intel belongs to the High Performance series, configured as an entry-level virtual server powered by a shared Intel Xeon processor. The hardware environment provides 1 vCPU with 1 physical core running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Memory capacity is fixed at 1.0 GB of RAM. The instance does not feature dedicated GPU acceleration, relying solely on CPU processing, but bundles 25 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU supports modern instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, along with AES hardware cryptographic acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate modest throughput, reflecting the single-core shared CPU allocation. In synthetic evaluations, stress-ng recorded 1421.08 points in single-core performance (middle 50%), while overall multi-core performance placed in the bottom 10%. Memory read bandwidth on large uncached blocks reached 9.16 GB/sec, with write bandwidth achieving 7.89 GB/sec. Application testing shows 1.58 million Redis SET operations per second and static web serving throughput of 1.37 GB/sec. Compression testing showed single-threaded gzip at 23.84 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 8.95 GB/sec.

This server represents a budget-friendly deployment option suited for low-overhead tasks rather than data-intensive computing. Primary tradeoffs include the strict 1.0 GB RAM constraint and shared CPU scheduling, which cap multi-threaded capacity and heavy database caching. It functions efficiently as a lightweight staging environment, low-traffic web host, microservice node, or small utility server where dense resource provisioning is unnecessary.
